title: Static Pods & Control Plane Troubleshooting
intro: On a kubeadm cluster, the control plane itself (kube-apiserver, scheduler, controller-manager, etcd) runs as static pods managed directly by kubelet — not by the API server. When kubectl itself won't connect, this is where you look.

steps.prompt: kubectl commands are hanging entirely — you suspect the API server isn't running. List the static pod manifests kubelet reads directly.
steps.explanation: If kube-apiserver.yaml is missing or invalid, kubectl can't reach the cluster at all — and since kubectl itself depends on the API server, you can't use kubectl to check on the thing that would tell you why kubectl is broken.
steps.why: This is the one situation where you're not using kubectl to investigate a kubectl problem — you go straight to the node's filesystem, since kubelet reads these files independent of whether the API server is up.

steps.prompt: Check the kube-apiserver static pod manifest for an obvious mistake, like a bad flag.
steps.explanation: '--bad-flag-typo=true' isn't a real kube-apiserver flag — kubelet will keep restarting this static pod in a crash loop as long as it's there.
steps.why: A typo'd flag here is a classic self-inflicted outage during manual cluster maintenance — it's also exactly why you always back up a manifest before hand-editing it, so you can revert in seconds instead of debugging under pressure.

steps.prompt: Since kubectl can't reach the API server, check the kubelet's own logs on this node instead to confirm it's actually retrying the static pod.
steps.fake_output:
kubelet: E0927 10:00:05 Error: failed to start container "kube-apiserver": unknown flag: --bad-flag-typo
kubelet: I0927 10:00:06 Restarting failed static pod kube-apiserver
steps.explanation: kubelet logs live in the system journal, not in anything kubectl can show you — this confirms kubelet is looping on the exact flag error from the manifest.
steps.why: This is the same shift as the manifest step: once the control plane itself is the thing that's broken, you're debugging at the systemd/kubelet layer on the actual node, not at the Kubernetes API layer.

steps.prompt: Fix the typo by removing the bad flag from the manifest, then confirm the API server static pod recovers.
steps.fake_output:
NAME                       READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
kube-apiserver-master      1/1     Running   0          15s
steps.explanation: As soon as you save a corrected manifest, kubelet picks up the change automatically and restarts the static pod — and once the API server is healthy again, kubectl starts working normally too.
steps.why: This closes the loop: you dropped down to file/journal-level debugging specifically because kubectl was unusable, and the fix at that lower level is what brings kubectl back.
